1#א: Even if it is forbidden for benefit — and if a piece worthy of honor that is forbidden for benefit became mixed among several pieces that are permitted for benefit but nevertheless forbidden for eating — whether in that respect too it is not nullified and all are forbidden for benefit — see Pleiti.
1#ב: For if it were to be nullified, and if it is a piece worthy of honor, and were it nullified there would no longer be a piece worthy of honor — nevertheless it is not nullified. See Pleiti.
1#ג: And even if it is forbidden only by d'rabbanan authority — see Pleiti, where I deliberated and concluded that regarding a d'rabbanan prohibition that involves only a prohibition of eating, there is room to argue for leniency when there is an additional basis to permit.
1#ד: This is a matter of doubt; see what I wrote below in siman 110.
2#א: Unless it is forbidden, etc. And if one curdled cheese with milk from a treifah animal: although cheese is a piece worthy of honor according to local custom, nevertheless the milk of a treifah animal is not a piece worthy of honor, and it is permitted — unless there is enough treifah milk within it that it alone would suffice to curdle the cheese, in which case the entire cheese is forbidden and constitutes a piece worthy of honor. The later authorities agreed to this. See Pleiti. And regarding cheeses of Eretz Yisrael — even though the prohibition is due to absorbed taste, which is itself forbidden, and even if one were to say that the absorbed material itself is permitted — nevertheless the rabbinic decree was to forbid the cheeses and treat them as the substance of the prohibition itself. See Pleiti, where I brought proof for this; see there.
2#ב: For the peel is not worthy of honor — even in basar b'chalav, where it was forbidden due to itself and not due to absorbed flavor.
2#ג: Worthy of honor. And if the peel itself alone is a piece worthy of honor — the opinion of the Peri Chadash, and so too it appears the opinion of the Shach, is that it is not nullified. See Pleiti, that one may be lenient.
3#א: For after it became mixed, since at the very moment it was mixed it was not yet a piece worthy of honor, it has already been nullified and is no longer significant enough to prohibit everything.
3#ב: And similarly a whole lamb — even if they have already been cooked, since before cooking it would not in any case be considered a piece worthy of honor. And if so, one must say that even if one has removed from it the sinews, the forbidden fats, and the membranes, it is still called a whole lamb with respect to nullification.
3#ג: A head, etc. But a head of a large animal implies that it is significant. The opinion of the Maharshal is that it is not significant. However, if the tongue is within it, the tongue is not nullified due to its significance, and the head does not diminish the tongue's significance.
4#_: A piece of fat-covered hide, etc. The opinion of Lechem Chamudot is that it is nullified. And it appears that even though they cut pieces from it and use them to honor guests, nevertheless it is not considered a piece worthy of honor — for no individual piece alone is worthy of honor, only many of them together. Therefore each individual piece is called not worthy of honor.
6#_: Or even when mixed with items not of the same species. The Issur V'Heter holds that the rule applies specifically when mixed with items of the same species. See Pleiti, where I deliberated on this matter and brought proofs in accordance with the words of the Issur V'Heter.
7#_: We do not attribute the identity probabilistically. Even though when a piece falls into the sea we do attribute its identity and say that the forbidden piece is the one that fell — because it is no longer in the world and we need not rule upon it — here, however, since they are all present in the world and we must rule on this piece as well, whether it is treifah or kosher, we do not attribute its status probabilistically.
8#_: We compare — see Pleiti: this applies specifically when one forbidden piece became mixed among two others, but if one became mixed among one, we do not rely on this comparison.
9#_: A lamb's head — the Bach [holds that regarding] a lamb's head in which liquid was found, and the bodies then became mixed together, one should examine the spinal cord: if liquid is found there, we attribute the identification to the body that had liquid in its head, since the liquid extended to the spine as well. The Taz, however, questioned this, since it is not found in any early authority.
